aspect: Paternal and maternal surnames, truncated or swapped
description: Systems storing a single surname take one, drop one, or reverse them, so the boarding pass, the visa and the degree certificate disagree.
energy_note: Four documents, three versions of his name.

aspect: Accents and ñ do not survive
description: Diacritics are stripped or mangled between systems, producing mismatches that airline and immigration software treats as discrepancies.
energy_note: An accent that becomes a red flag.

aspect: It reads as an attempt to deceive
description: A name discrepancy is interpreted as possible deception rather than as a known limitation of the software, which is what turns a data problem into a secondary inspection.
energy_note: A software limitation, treated as a lie.

description: Boarding pass: RAMIREZDELGADO/JOSE. Visa: Jose Ramirez. Degree: José Ramírez Delgado. Bank: Jose R Delgado. The officer lays them side by side and asks which one is his actual name. All of them are.
energy_note: Asked to pick which of his names is the real one.
